case_title: Baseline · STP off on the MLAG pair, RSTP on the access switch (campus option 1)
fault: Resets the data bridge on all three CHRs over management SSH: protocol-mode=none and forward-reserved-addresses=no on both MLAG peers, protocol-mode=rstp priority=0x0000 on the access switch, with edge=yes on its uplink bond and edge=yes, bpdu-guard=yes and loop-protect=on on its host port ether4, and reads the access switch port settings back. Then run numbered 100 ms pings for 4 s in both VLAN 110 and both bypass directions, read back bridge, MLAG, RSTP and LACP state, and send three ARP broadcasts each way. No fault is applied.
expected: Both MLAG peers run protocol-mode=none with forward-reserved-addresses=no, so they neither send BPDUs nor pass the access switch's BPDUs (STP group address 01:80:C2:00:00:00). The access switch is the only RSTP bridge and, with priority 0x0000, its own root (root ID 0x0000.02:00:00:21:00:13). Its uplink bond is an edge port, so it forwards at once without a proposal/agreement handshake, and its host port ether4 is an edge port with bpdu-guard=yes and loop-protect=on. MLAG is connected, every bond member is synchronized, collecting and distributing, each ARP broadcast arrives once and all four streams deliver with zero loss.

case_title: One-way calibration · STP off on the MLAG pair, RSTP on the access switch (campus option 1)
fault: After the campus option 1 bridge reset and baseline gate, the runner adds a tc ingress filter on host 2's eth3 that drops bypass-forward echo requests (stream 301) for 2 s. It then removes the filter and observes 3 s of settling and a 3 s recovery window.
expected: The filter drops only stream 301's echo requests at host 2's bypass port, outside the MLAG fabric. Stream 301 shows exactly one gap, with every request sent, and the gap's bounds enclose the measured 1.9–2.3 s filter interval. The reverse bypass and both VLAN 110 directions lose nothing.

case_title: MLAG secondary reboot · Medium lab, STP off on the MLAG pair, RSTP on the access switch (campus option 1)
fault: Resets the data bridge on all three CHRs over management SSH: protocol-mode=none and forward-reserved-addresses=no on both MLAG peers, protocol-mode=rstp priority=0x0000 on the access switch, with edge=yes on its uplink bond and edge=yes, bpdu-guard=yes and loop-protect=on on its host port ether4, and reads the access switch port settings back. It requires a loss-free probe baseline, no BPDU from or through the MLAG pair and one copy of each broadcast. It then reboots CHR 2 (MLAG secondary, mlag-priority=20) with `/system reboot`, waits for the guest uptime to reset and keeps probing for 16 s plus a 3 s recovery window.
expected: CHR 1 (MLAG primary) keeps the shared system ID, so the access switch's uplink bond and traffic host 2 keep their LACP partner and forward over their members to CHR 1. The virtual links keep carrier, so they drop the member to CHR 2 only at the LACP short timeout (3 × 1 s). The access switch stays its own RSTP root and its edge uplink keeps forwarding, because a member leaving the bond does not change the bridge port.

case_title: MLAG secondary power loss · Medium lab, STP off on the MLAG pair, RSTP on the access switch (campus option 1)
fault: Resets the data bridge on all three CHRs over management SSH: protocol-mode=none and forward-reserved-addresses=no on both MLAG peers, protocol-mode=rstp priority=0x0000 on the access switch, with edge=yes on its uplink bond and edge=yes, bpdu-guard=yes and loop-protect=on on its host port ether4, and reads the access switch port settings back. It requires a loss-free probe baseline, no BPDU from or through the MLAG pair and one copy of each broadcast. It then emulates a power loss of CHR 2 (MLAG secondary): in one step it takes the container veths behind CHR 2's ether2 to ether4 down, sets the facing NICs of CHR 1 and the access switch link-down over QMP and pauses CHR 2's guest with QMP stop, then confirms carrier loss at every neighbour. After 20 s it powers CHR 2 on with QMP system_reset and cont, brings the links back up, waits for the guest uptime to reset and keeps probing for 16 s plus a 3 s recovery window.
expected: Every link to CHR 2 loses carrier at once, as on a real power loss. CHR 1 (MLAG primary) sees its peer port ether2 go down and keeps the shared system ID, so the access switch's uplink bond and traffic host 2 keep their LACP partner. They drop their member to CHR 2 on carrier loss, without waiting for the LACP short timeout. The uplink bond keeps one running member, so the access switch's edge bridge port keeps forwarding.

case_title: Inter-pair bond member flap · two MLAG pairs, spanning tree off
fault: Resets the data bridge on all four CHRs over management SSH with protocol-mode=none. Pair A (CHR 1 MLAG primary, CHR 2 MLAG secondary) and pair B (CHR 3 MLAG primary, CHR 4 MLAG secondary) are joined by one distributed LACP bond, mlag-id 11 on pair A and 21 on pair B. Host 1 bonds to pair B and host 2 to pair A, so both VLAN 110 streams cross both pairs. It requires a loss-free baseline. It then takes the inter-pair bond member between CHR 1 ether3 and CHR 3 ether3 down at both ends (both container veths and both QEMU NICs), holds it down for 8 s, brings both ends back up and watches 8 s of return plus a 3 s recovery window. The bridge host table size and the topology-change counter of every CHR are sampled throughout.
expected: CHR 1 and CHR 3 each lose their only member of the inter-pair MLAG bond (mlag-id 11 on pair A, 21 on pair B). The bond keeps forwarding over its other member between CHR 2 and CHR 4, and traffic that reaches CHR 1 or CHR 3 crosses its pair's peer port. Streams 101 and 201 lose at most 3 s. No bridge sends or forwards BPDUs. The field report saw unrelated MACs move to the peer port and the host table shrink after this flap; the host table size and topology-change counter of every CHR are recorded for comparison.

case_title: One-way calibration · two MLAG pairs, spanning tree off
fault: After the bridge reset (protocol-mode=none) and baseline gate, the runner adds a tc ingress filter on host 2's eth3 that drops bypass-forward echo requests (stream 301) for 2 s. It then removes the filter and observes 3 s of settling and a 3 s recovery window.
expected: The filter drops only stream 301's echo requests at host 2's bypass port, outside both MLAG pairs. Stream 301 shows exactly one gap, with every request sent, and the gap's bounds enclose the measured 1.9–2.3 s filter interval. The reverse bypass and both VLAN 110 directions lose nothing.

case_title: Pair A primary reboot · two MLAG pairs, spanning tree off

case_title: Baseline · STP off on the MLAG pair, RSTP on the access switch (campus option 1)
fault: Resets the data bridge on all three CHRs over management SSH: protocol-mode=none and forward-reserved-addresses=no on both MLAG peers, protocol-mode=rstp priority=0x0000 on the access switch, with edge=yes on its uplink bond and edge=yes, bpdu-guard=yes and loop-protect=on on its host port ether4, and reads the access switch port settings back. Then run numbered 100 ms pings for 4 s in both VLAN 110 and both bypass directions, read back bridge, MLAG, RSTP and LACP state, and send three ARP broadcasts each way. No fault is applied.
expected: Both MLAG peers run protocol-mode=none with forward-reserved-addresses=no, so they neither send BPDUs nor pass the access switch's BPDUs (STP group address 01:80:C2:00:00:00). The access switch is the only RSTP bridge and, with priority 0x0000, its own root (root ID 0x0000.02:00:00:21:00:13). Its uplink bond is an edge port, so it forwards at once without a proposal/agreement handshake, and its host port ether4 is an edge port with bpdu-guard=yes and loop-protect=on. MLAG is connected, every bond member is synchronized, collecting and distributing, each ARP broadcast arrives once and all four streams deliver with zero loss.

expected: Both MLAG peers lose ICCP and leave mlag-state connected. With mlag-lacp-fallback=yes the MLAG secondary stops using the shared system ID, so the clients renegotiate LACP and keep their member to the primary, with brief loss.

case_title: Peer link loss and return
fault: Cuts the peer link (ether2) at both MLAG peers, holds it down for 15 s, restores it and watches 65 s of return.
expected: ICCP returns to mlag-state connected on both peers and the secondary takes the shared system ID again. The clients renegotiate LACP with brief loss.

case_title: MAC move between MLAG peers and back
fault: Switches the MAC-move host's active-backup bond from its link to CHR 1 to its link to CHR 2, keeping the same MAC and IP address, then switches it back after 4 s.
expected: The host's gratuitous ARP enters CHR 2 on ether5, a regular bridge port without mlag-id. CHR 2 moves the host MAC to ether5 in its bridge host table and floods the broadcast to its local ports and over the peer port; CHR 1 floods it only to its regular port ether5 and moves the MAC to the peer port ether2. Lab target: no probe to or from the host is lost, and once the gratuitous ARP reaches CHR 2, no frame addressed to the host MAC leaves CHR 1 on ether5.

case_title: MAC move between MLAG peers and back
fault: Switches the MAC-move host's active-backup bond from its link to CHR 1 to its link to CHR 2, keeping the same MAC and IP address, then switches it back after 4 s.

CHR 1 moves the host MAC back to ether5 and floods the broadcast to its local ports and over the peer port; CHR 2 floods it only to its regular port ether5 and moves the MAC to the peer port ether2. Lab target: no probe to or from the host is lost, and from the moment the gratuitous ARP reaches CHR 1 to the end of the recovery window, no frame addressed to the host MAC leaves CHR 2 on ether5.

case_title: Repeated MLAG bond member flap
fault: Takes client 1's bond member to CHR 1 (ether3) down at both ends for 1 s and back up for 3 s, five times, then watches 8 s of return plus a 3 s recovery window. Both MLAG peers' bridge host table entries for client 2 and the MAC-move host are sampled every 0.35 s throughout.
expected: Each flap removes ether3 from CHR 1's MLAG bond client1 and adds it back once LACP renegotiates. While the member is down, CHR 1 forwards traffic for client 1 over the peer link to CHR 2, with brief loss. This phase runs from the first flap to the fifth return, so it holds four complete flaps and the fifth down; result.json lists the loss of every flap separately. Each loss of streams 101, 201 and 302 may last at most 3 s, the member limit per flap. Streams 102 and 202 never touch client 1 and lose nothing, and the bridge host table entries for client 2 and the MAC-move host stay on both MLAG peers. The field report saw unrelated MACs move to the peer port after a member flap.
failed_checks: 501 broadcast from client 1: no second sighting at the sender's bond members during withdrawal, seq [120]
502 unknown unicast from client 1: no second sighting at the sender's bond members during withdrawal, seq [120, 204]

case_title: Baseline readiness
fault: Applies the bridge mode on both MLAG peers, waits for MLAG and LACP to settle, checks MLAG, LACP and the virtual links, and sends numbered pings for 4 s without a fault.
expected: Both MLAG peers show mlag-state connected, one as MLAG primary and one as MLAG secondary, and use the primary's system ID as the shared system ID. Each client bonds both members and every probe arrives once.

case_title: Calibration before reboots
fault: Runs the baseline check, then drops the forward bypass pings at client 2 for 2 s with a tc filter while four numbered ping streams run.
expected: Only the bypass stream between the two clients loses probes, and its measured gap contains the applied 1.9–2.3 s cut. The bypass does not cross the MLAG peers, so every other stream loses nothing.

case_title: MLAG secondary reboot
fault: Resets the bridge on CHR 1 and CHR 2 over management SSH with the bridge mode of the run, picks the MLAG peer that reports mlag-state connected as secondary, and after a loss-free baseline reboots it with `/system reboot` (1 s delay). The runner waits for the guest uptime to reset, then keeps probing for 16 s plus a 3 s recovery window.
expected: The MLAG primary keeps the shared system ID, so both traffic hosts keep their LACP partner and forward over their bond member to the primary, which delivers locally without the peer port. The virtual links keep carrier, so each host drops its member to the secondary only at the LACP short timeout (3 × 1 s). Only traffic hashed to that member sees brief loss.

case_title: MLAG secondary reboot

case_title: MLAG secondary power loss
fault: Resets the bridge on CHR 1 and CHR 2 over management SSH with the bridge mode of the run, picks the MLAG peer that reports mlag-state connected as secondary, and after a loss-free baseline emulates its power loss. In one step it takes the container veths behind the secondary's ether2 to ether5 down, sets the other peer's peer-link NIC link-down over QMP and pauses the secondary's guest with QMP stop, then confirms carrier loss at every neighbour. After 20 s it powers the secondary on with QMP system_reset and cont, brings the links back up, waits for the guest uptime to reset and keeps probing for 16 s plus a 3 s recovery window.
expected: Every link to the secondary loses carrier at once, as on a real power loss. The MLAG primary sees its peer port ether2 go down and keeps the shared system ID, so both traffic hosts keep their LACP partner. Each host drops its member to the secondary on carrier loss, without waiting for the LACP short timeout, and forwards over its member to the primary. Only traffic hashed to the lost member sees brief loss.

case_title: Baseline · MSTP, MLAG pair as root
fault: Reset the data bridge on all three CHRs over management SSH with protocol-mode=mstp, priority 0x1000 on both MLAG peers and 0x8000 on the access switch. Then run numbered 100 ms pings for 4 s in both VLAN 110 and both bypass directions and read back bridge, MLAG, RSTP and LACP state. No fault is applied.
expected: Both MLAG peers are connected and use the MLAG primary's system ID as the shared RSTP bridge ID, so both show as root bridge with root ID 0x1000.02:00:00:21:00:11. The access switch picks its non-edge uplink bond as root port and all VLAN 110 ports forward. RSTP BPDUs from that root reach the access switch, and all four streams deliver with zero loss.

case_title: One-way calibration · MSTP, MLAG pair as root
fault: After the RSTP pair-root bridge reset and baseline gate, the runner adds a tc ingress filter on host 2's eth3 that drops bypass-forward echo requests (stream 301) for 2 s. It then removes the filter and observes 3 s of settling and a 3 s recovery window.
expected: The filter drops only stream 301's echo requests at host 2's bypass port, outside the MLAG fabric. Stream 301 shows exactly one gap, with every request sent, and the gap's bounds enclose the measured 1.9–2.3 s filter interval. The reverse bypass and both VLAN 110 directions lose nothing.

case_title: MLAG secondary reboot · Medium lab, MSTP, MLAG pair as root
fault: Resets all three bridges over management SSH with protocol-mode=mstp, priority 0x1000 on CHR 1 and CHR 2 and 0x8000 on the access switch. It requires a loss-free baseline with root ID 0x1000.02:00:00:21:00:11 in the access switch's BPDUs. It then reboots CHR 2 (MLAG secondary) with `/system reboot`, waits for the guest uptime to reset and keeps probing for 16 s plus a 3 s recovery window.
expected: CHR 1 keeps the shared system ID, which is both the RSTP bridge ID and the LACP system ID, so the access switch still sees root 0x1000.02:00:00:21:00:11 and its uplink stays the forwarding root port. The virtual links keep carrier, so the access switch and traffic host 2 drop their member to CHR 2 at the LACP short timeout (3 × 1 s). Only traffic hashed to that member sees brief loss.

expected: The filter drops only stream 301's echo requests at host 2's bypass port, outside the MLAG fabric. Stream 301 shows exactly one gap, with every request sent, and the gap's bounds enclose the measured 1.9–2.3 s filter interval. The reverse bypass and both VLAN 110 directions lose nothing.

case_title: MLAG secondary reboot · Medium lab, MSTP, MLAG pair as root
fault: Resets all three bridges over management SSH with protocol-mode=mstp, priority 0x1000 on CHR 1 and CHR 2 and 0x8000 on the access switch. It requires a loss-free baseline with root ID 0x1000.02:00:00:21:00:11 in the access switch's BPDUs. It then reboots CHR 2 (MLAG secondary) with `/system reboot`, waits for the guest uptime to reset and keeps probing for 16 s plus a 3 s recovery window.
expected: CHR 1 keeps the shared system ID, which is both the RSTP bridge ID and the LACP system ID, so the access switch still sees root 0x1000.02:00:00:21:00:11 and its uplink stays the forwarding root port. The virtual links keep carrier, so the access switch and traffic host 2 drop their member to CHR 2 at the LACP short timeout (3 × 1 s). Only traffic hashed to that member sees brief loss.

case_title: MLAG secondary reboot · Medium lab, MSTP, MLAG pair as root
fault: Resets all three bridges over management SSH with protocol-mode=mstp, priority 0x1000 on CHR 1 and CHR 2 and 0x8000 on the access switch. It requires a loss-free baseline with root ID 0x1000.02:00:00:21:00:11 in the access switch's BPDUs. It then reboots CHR 2 (MLAG secondary) with `/system reboot`, waits for the guest uptime to reset and keeps probing for 16 s plus a 3 s recovery window.
expected: CHR 2 keeps its bond members out of the bond until the MLAG system ID syncs (mlag-init-delay), then adds them under the unchanged shared system ID. The root ID and the access switch's forwarding uplink do not change, so loss is brief or none.

case_title: Baseline · two MLAG pairs, equal bridge priority 0x8000
fault: Resets the data bridge on all four CHRs over management SSH with protocol-mode=rstp and bridge priority 0x8000 on all four CHRs, as in the field report where every MLAG pair kept the same priority. Pair A (CHR 1 MLAG primary, CHR 2 MLAG secondary) and pair B (CHR 3 MLAG primary, CHR 4 MLAG secondary) are joined by one distributed LACP bond, mlag-id 11 on pair A and 21 on pair B. Host 1 bonds to pair B and host 2 to pair A, so both VLAN 110 streams cross both pairs. Then runs numbered 100 ms pings for 4 s in both VLAN 110 and both bypass directions and reads back bridge, MLAG, RSTP and LACP state on all four CHRs. No fault is applied.
expected: Both pairs are connected and each presents its MLAG primary's bridge ID: pair A 0x8000.02:00:00:21:00:11, pair B 0x8000.02:00:00:21:00:12. All four CHRs report root 0x8000.02:00:00:21:00:11; pair A wins on the lower bridge MAC, because all priorities are equal. Every member of the inter-pair bond and both host bonds is synchronized, collecting and distributing, RSTP BPDUs from the root reach pair B, and all four streams deliver with zero loss.

fault: After the bridge reset (bridge priority 0x8000 on all four CHRs, as in the field report where every MLAG pair kept the same priority) and baseline gate, the runner adds a tc ingress filter on host 2's eth3 that drops bypass-forward echo requests (stream 301) for 2 s. It then removes the filter and observes 3 s of settling and a 3 s recovery window.
expected: The filter drops only stream 301's echo requests at host 2's bypass port, outside both MLAG pairs. Stream 301 shows exactly one gap, with every request sent, and the gap's bounds enclose the measured 1.9–2.3 s filter interval. The reverse bypass and both VLAN 110 directions lose nothing.

case_title: Pair A primary reboot · two MLAG pairs, equal bridge priority 0x8000
fault: Resets the data bridge on all four CHRs over management SSH with protocol-mode=rstp and bridge priority 0x8000 on all four CHRs, as in the field report where every MLAG pair kept the same priority. Pair A (CHR 1 MLAG primary, CHR 2 MLAG secondary) and pair B (CHR 3 MLAG primary, CHR 4 MLAG secondary) are joined by one distributed LACP bond, mlag-id 11 on pair A and 21 on pair B. Host 1 bonds to pair B and host 2 to pair A, so both VLAN 110 streams cross both pairs. It requires a loss-free baseline with root 0x8000.02:00:00:21:00:11 on all four CHRs. It then reboots CHR 1 (pair A's MLAG primary) with `/system reboot`, waits for the guest uptime to reset and keeps probing for 16 s plus a 3 s recovery window.
